items.prompt: In the simplified model with P=120 million, t=0.20 and N=30 million, calculate after-tax earnings and EPS. Show all steps.

rubric.criterion: Divide by share count with correct EPS and units

items.solution: Tax expense = 120×0.20 = 24 million; after-tax earnings = 120−24 = 96 million; EPS = 96/30 = 3.20 currency units per share.

items.prompt: Explain why reducing t from 0.30 to 0.25 does not increase EPS by exactly 5%, and compute the actual relative increase with P and N fixed.

rubric.criterion: Explain fixed P and N assumptions

items.solution: The rate decreased by 0.05, which equals 5 percentage points. Relative change in EPS is (0.75−0.70)/0.70 = 0.05/0.70 ≈ 7.14%. The denominator is original after-tax earnings, not the original tax rate.

items.prompt: Two scenarios share pretax profit P=80 million and N=10 million shares: Scenario A has t=0.28; B has t=0.24. Compare EPS, identify which scenario has higher EPS and explain one reason this stylized ranking need not imply a larger real-world company valuation.
items.solution: EPS_A=80×0.72/10=5.76. EPS_B=80×0.76/10=6.08, so Scenario B has 0.32 more EPS. Valuation can depend on future growth, risk, financial-reporting assumptions and many other inputs, so EPS alone does not establish company value.
